John Hurt: Top 10 Movies Ranked

26 April 2024 · RewindZone Archive

When it comes to versatile actors, John Hurt is a name that always comes up. With a career spanning over five decades, Hurt has delivered some truly unforgettable performances. In this article, we're going to take a look at his top 10 movies, ranked.

Dead Man (1995) - John Scholfield

Starting off our list is Jim Jarmusch's "Dead Man," where Hurt plays the role of John Scholfield. This film is a gem, and Hurt's role as Scholfield adds so much to its quirky charm. Hurt brings this philosophical depth to Scholfield that really complements the film's offbeat Western vibe. His scenes with Johnny Depp's character are just mesmerising; you can feel the weight of their conversations.

Rob Roy (1995) - John Graham, Marquis of Montrose

Advertisement

Next up, we have "Rob Roy," where Hurt is just magnetic as John Graham, Marquis of Montrose. The way he embodies this historical figure with such authority and complexity is captivating. It's one of those performances that stays with you long after the film ends.

Watership Down (1978) - Hazel (Voice)

Now, "Watership Down" is a childhood favourite for many, and Hurt's voice work as Hazel is simply iconic. He brings this warmth and wisdom to the character, that makes Hazel the heart of the story. It's amazing how much emotion he conveys just through his voice.

White Mischief (1987) - Gilbert Colvile

"White Mischief" is such a fascinating film, and Hurt's portrayal of Gilbert Colvile is a standout. He plays this morally ambiguous character with such nuance, adding layers to the film's intrigue and drama. It's a role that really showcases Hurt's versatility.

10 Rillington Place (1971) - Timothy John Evans

"10 Rillington Place" is a haunting film, and Hurt's performance as Timothy John Evans is truly haunting. He captures the tragedy and injustice of Evans' story with such raw emotion. It's a gripping performance that keeps you on the edge of your seat.

Snowpiercer (2013) - Gilliam

Advertisement

"Snowpiercer" is such a wild ride, and Hurt's character, Gilliam, is this wise old sage guiding the protagonists through this dystopian world. Hurt brings this mysterious aura to Gilliam that adds so much depth to the character. You can't help but be drawn into his wisdom and gravitas.

1984 (1984) - Winston Smith

Ah, "1984"! Hurt's portrayal of Winston Smith is absolutely chilling. He captures Smith's fear and defiance against this oppressive regime with such intensity. It's a performance that really makes you feel the weight of Orwell's dystopian vision.

Alien (1979) - Engineer G.W. Kane

"Alien" is a sci-fi classic, and Hurt's role as Engineer G.W. Kane is unforgettable. That chest-bursting scene? Iconic. Hurt brings this vulnerability and humanity to Kane, that makes his character's fate all the more heartbreaking.

Midnight Express (1978) - Max

In "Midnight Express," Hurt plays Max, a fellow prisoner who forms this complex bond with the protagonist. Hurt's portrayal adds this layer of grit and realism to the film's portrayal of life in a Turkish prison. It's a performance that really resonates with you.

John Hurt was a true talent, and these ten movies showcase his incredible range and depth as an actor. From voice work to leading roles, Hurt always brought something special to the table. Whether you're a fan of his work or just discovering it for the first time, these movies are a must-watch.

  • What was John Hurt's most iconic role?John Hurt had many iconic roles, but his portrayal of John Merrick in "The Elephant Man" is often considered his most iconic.
  • Did John Hurt win any awards for his acting?Yes, John Hurt won numerous awards for his acting, including two BAFTA Awards and a Golden Globe.
  • What was John Hurt's last movie?John Hurt's last movie was "That Good Night," which was released in 2017.
  • Did John Hurt do his own stunts in "Alien"?No, John Hurt did not do his own stunts in "Alien." The famous chestburster scene was performed using a fake torso and a puppet.
  • What was John Hurt's favorite role?John Hurt once said that his favorite role was playing Quentin Crisp in "The Naked Civil Servant" and "An Englishman in New York."
